quote.text: People of the same trade seldom meet together, even for merriment and diversion, but the conversation ends in a conspiracy against the public, or in some contrivance to raise prices.
quote.author: Adam Smith, An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations, Book I, Chapter X, 1776

stories.headline: Anthropic files to list on Nasdaq, compute bill left blank
stories.dek: The S-1 of 26 October gives first-half revenue as US$16.3bn and states the aggregate compute commitment four times as “more than $ ” — and leaves the third-quarter revenue figure blank in three places too.

stories.headline: A survey of 5,439 printers by Ilford blames cost and space
stories.dek: The answers Ilford got were cost and space, not mystique — and 86 per cent of non-printers said they would try it if that one obstacle were removed.

stories.headline: Australia banned card surcharges; Macquarie’s DEFT stopped taking cards
stories.dek: From 1 October the fee had to vanish from every Australian receipt. Where a price could be raised it rose about eight times the fee; where it could not — rent, strata levies, the tax bill — the card was withdrawn instead.

stories.headline: Israel’s record turnout leaves neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot a majority
stories.dek: Exit polls put Netanyahu’s bloc on 50 seats and Gadi Eisenkot’s on 52 to 53, with Arab parties at a record 17 — and not one ballot had been counted when this page was set.

stories.headline: The retirement age in Singapore moves to 65 in January 2029
stories.dek: The Tripartite Workgroup’s six recommendations, all accepted by Government on 26 October, also lift re-employment to 70 and replace the Senior Employment Credit with a Re-Employment Credit paying up to 7 per cent of wages.

stories.headline: Ferguson’s of Banbridge says no other house still weaves double damask
stories.dek: A 175cm loom width caps every tablecloth the serious mills make, thread counts top out near 202 rather than 1,000, and Matouk’s US$550 linen cloth is sewn in the Philippines from Italian fabric.

stories.headline: Samsung’s Galaxy Buds On reach Korea at 299,000 won
stories.dek: Samsung’s first clip-on open-ear bud went on sale on 27 October with 9.5 hours of playback and no published water rating — and two outlets are already printing an IP54 figure Samsung never gave.

stories.headline: Breitling puts a hand-wound movement in the core Navitimer at S$10,450
stories.dek: The B09 Chronograph 41, launched on 22 October, is chronometer-certified with a 70-hour reserve — and is already on sale at six different public prices, two of which contradict each other inside one review.

stories.headline: Waititi’s Klara and the Sun opens to $701,059 from 880 theatres
stories.dek: The $20m Ishiguro adaptation took a Sunday per-theatre average of $198 and drew zero positive notices on Metacritic, while Wicker, made for $10m, took $5.75m at 95 per cent on Rotten Tomatoes.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · A Singapore Reanalysis
stories.headline: Bavelier’s team re-reads 3,434 Singapore pupils: hours did not predict harm
stories.dek: In PLoS One on 21 October, a reanalysis of a 2007–09 schools cohort finds that among the heaviest gamers — averaging 57 hours a week — change in impulse control explained the symptoms, not change in playing time.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · The Real Yield
stories.headline: The US ten-year closed at 4.99, the real yield at 2.64
stories.dek: Treasury’s own curves put the ten-year breakeven at 2.35 on 27 October with Brent at $114.22 — the market is pricing the oil shock as temporary and charging the whole cost to the real rate.

stories.headline: A Singapore meta-analysis finds staking money adds 665 steps a day
stories.dek: Published in the European Journal of Preventive Cardiology on 26 October, the pooled estimate across 29 randomised trials has a confidence interval of 463 to 867 steps and heterogeneity of zero.

stories.kicker: The Diary · One Date That Matters
stories.headline: Advance sales for Tokyo’s January sumo tournament open on 5 December
stories.dek: The November tournament in Fukuoka is already sold out on all fifteen days, which is the evidence that the 5 December window is the one to diary — and Wild Rice opens Monkey Goes West on 12 November.
